requirement: Cyprus Investment Firms must not offer bonuses designed to incentivise retail clients to trade in complex speculative products such as CFDs, binary options, and rolling spot forex.
source_quote: CIFs must avoid the practice of offering bonuses that are designed to incentivise retail clients to trade in complex speculative products such as CFDs, binary options and rolling spot forex as it is unlikely that a firm offering such bonuses could demonstrate that it is acting honestly, fairly and professionally and in the best interests of its retail clients [article 36(1) of the Investment Services and Activities and Regulated Markets Law, ‘the Law’].

requirement: Bonuses that are return of an amount (e.g., welcome bonuses, volume bonuses, refer-a-friend bonuses) which cannot be withdrawn until a target volume is reached are examples of bonuses that are not permissible if they incentivise trading in complex speculative products.
source_quote: An amount of money or a percentage on the initial or/and additional deposit of the client, which cannot be withdrawn until a target volume has been reached... An amount of money based on the trades the client executes, which cannot be withdrawn until a target volume has been reached... An amount of money or percentage of the referred “friend’s” initial deposit, which cannot be withdrawn until a target volume has been reached.

requirement: Offering lower spreads as a reward to clients instead of return of an amount is permissible and not considered a violation of article 36(1) of the Law.
source_quote: If a CIF wishes to reward its clients, it can offer to them for example lower spreads instead of a return of an amount, as the example 8 in Appendix 1 (cash rebates). In this case, the CIF is not considered that is violating the article 36(1) of the Law.

requirement: Marketing and promotional material must not be produced by Staff who communicate with clients about services and products, as such production is excluded from the scope of this circular.
source_quote: This circular does not apply to persons who only: ... v. Produce marketing and promotional material.

requirement: Staff must not use frequent and repeated telephone calls, aggressive language, or exert pressure urging or advising clients to invest or deposit funds in communications with clients.
source_quote: CIFs must ensure that practices such as frequent and repeated telephone calls to clients initiated by the Staff, and/or the use of aggressive language, and/or the exercising of pressure, urging/advising the client e.g. to invest and/or to deposit funds, are not and must not be employed/used by the Staff.

requirement: Staff must use their real name and not an alias, and must not give false information regarding their credentials when communicating with clients.
source_quote: CIFs must ensure that the Staff uses its real name and not an alias, and does not give false information regarding its credentials, when communicating with clients.

requirement: Marketing materials, promotions, client communications, bonuses, rewards, or financial incentives must provide costs and charges information that is fair, clear, and not misleading.
source_quote: The focus of the CSA will be on information provided to retail clients. NCAs, in particular, will review how firms ensure that these disclosures: are fair, clear and not misleading;

requirement: Costs and charges disclosed in marketing materials, promotions, client communications, bonuses, rewards, or financial incentives must be based on accurate data reflecting all explicit and implicit costs and charges.
source_quote: NCAs, in particular, will review how firms ensure that these disclosures: are based on accurate data reflecting all explicit and implicit costs and charges;

requirement: Marketing materials, promotions, client communications, bonuses, rewards, or financial incentives must adequately disclose any inducements.
source_quote: NCAs, in particular, will review how firms ensure that these disclosures: adequately disclose inducements.

requirement: CFD providers must not use incentives when marketing CFDs to retail clients.
source_quote: ESMA’s measures consist of restrictions to the marketing, distribution or sale of CFDs to retail clients and include: ... preventing the use of incentives by a CFD provider;

requirement: CFD providers must not use any form of promotional language that incentivises, induces or pressures a retail client to request to be treated as a professional client.
source_quote: investment firms should strictly refrain from implementing any form of practice that incentivises, induces or pressures an investor to request to be treated as a professional client. In this respect, any form of promotional language in relation to the status of professional client shall be seen as incentivising a retail client to request a professional client status.

requirement: CFD providers must not use promotional language that compares leverage limits available to different types of clients as this qualifies as incentivisation.
source_quote: ESMA considers that providing a comparison between leverage limits available to different types of clients would qualify as an incentivisation.

requirement: CFD providers must not promise or provide any form of monetary or non-monetary benefit as a reward for becoming a professional client.
source_quote: the promise or the provision of any form of monetary or non-monetary benefit as a “reward” for becoming a professional client will be seen as an inappropriate practice.

requirement: Third-country CFD providers must not market CFDs to retail clients in the Union that do not comply with ESMA’s or national product intervention measures.
source_quote: CFD providers are not allowed to market CFDs to retail clients in the Union that do not comply with the requirements from ESMA’s or national product intervention measures.

requirement: Marketing or incentivising language about the possibility to open an account with a third-country entity offering CFDs with higher leverage limits is prohibited as it constitutes marketing towards clients located in the EU.
source_quote: Promotional or incentivising language about the possibility to open an account with a third-country entity shall be seen as a marketing towards the client located in the EU, for example marketing the possibility to open an account where CFDs with higher leverage limits can be traded.

requirement: CFD providers must not offer, directly or indirectly, any payment, monetary or non-monetary benefit (other than information and research tools related to CFDs) as an incentive to retail investors to trade CFDs.
source_quote: CFD providers will be required not to provide, directly or indirectly, retail investors with a payment, monetary or excluded non-monetary benefit (i.e. any non-monetary benefit other than, insofar as they relate to CFDs, information and research tools) in relation to the marketing, distribution or sale of a CFD, other than the realised profits on any CFD provided.

requirement: All communications relating to the marketing, distribution or sale of CFDs to retail investors must include an appropriate risk warning that states the percentage of the provider's retail investor CFD trading accounts that lost money over the last 12 months.
source_quote: CFD providers will not be allowed to send, directly or indirectly, a communication to or publish information accessible by a retail investor relating to the marketing, distribution or sale of a CFD unless it includes an appropriate risk warning. In the risk warning, each CFD provider will be required to provide the percentage of its retail investor CFD trading accounts that lost money over the last 12-month period.

requirement: Marketing, distribution or sale of binary options to retail investors is prohibited.
source_quote: The product intervention measure ESMA has agreed under Article 40 of MiFIR is a prohibition on the marketing, distribution or sale of binary options to retail investors.

requirement: All information, including marketing communication, addressed to clients or potential clients shall be fair, clear and not misleading.
source_quote: all information, including marketing communication, addressed by CIFs to their clients or potential clients, shall be fair, clear and not misleading (section 36(1)(a) of Investment Services and Activities and Regulated Markets Law of 2007 as amended)

requirement: Marketing communication must use prominent bold type styles for important information, statements or warnings.
source_quote: Important information, statements or warnings are prominent using bold type styles.

requirement: Marketing communication must balance both the benefits and drawbacks of a financial product/service through equally prominent features.
source_quote: Both the benefits and drawbacks of a financial product/service are balanced through equally prominent features.

requirement: Risk warnings in marketing communication must be contained within their own distinct border to draw the reader’s attention.
source_quote: Risk warnings are contained within their own distinct border, thus drawing the reader’s attention to them.

requirement: Risk warnings must be clearly stated within the main body of the marketing communication and ahead of the ‘small print’.
source_quote: Risk warnings are clearly stated within the main body of the marketing communication and ahead of the ‘small print’ (i.e. legal text or contact information)

requirement: Risk information must appear on the website home page that the customer first arrives at when following a promotional link.
source_quote: Risk information appears on the website home page of CIFs that the customer first arrives at, when following a promotional link.

requirement: Marketing communication must include a risk warning wording such as: 'the investment value can both increase and decrease and the investors may lose all their invested capital'.
source_quote: use wording such as the following: ‘the investment value can both increase and decrease and the investors may lose all their invested capital’.

requirement: For leverage products, marketing communication must emphasize that losses may be more than the invested capital.
source_quote: in case of a leverage product, CIFs should emphasize that “loses may be more than the invested capital”.

requirement: Marketing information must include the name of the investment firm (IF).
source_quote: The information: (a) shall include the name of the IF;

requirement: Marketing information shall not emphasize potential benefits without also giving a fair and prominent indication of any relevant risks.
source_quote: shall not emphasize any potential benefits of an investment service or financial instrument without also giving a fair and prominent indication of any relevant risks;

requirement: Marketing information must be sufficient for and presented in a way likely to be understood by the average member of the target group.
source_quote: shall be sufficient for, and presented in a way that is likely to be understood by, the average member of the group to whom it is directed, or by whom it is likely to be received;

requirement: Marketing information shall not disguise, diminish or obscure important items, statements or warnings.
source_quote: shall not disguise, diminish or obscure important items, statements or warnings

requirement: Where marketing information compares investment or ancillary services, financial instruments, or providers, the comparison must be meaningful and presented in a fair and balanced way.
source_quote: the comparison must be meaningful and presented in a fair and balanced way;

requirement: Marketing information that compares services or products must specify the sources of the information used for the comparison.
source_quote: the sources of the information used for the comparison must be specified;

requirement: Marketing information that compares services or products must include the key facts and assumptions used to make the comparison.
source_quote: the key facts and assumptions used to make the comparison must be included.

requirement: Where marketing information contains an indication of past performance, it must not be the most prominent feature of the communication.
source_quote: that indication must not be the most prominent feature of the communication;

requirement: Past performance information must cover the immediately preceding 5 years or the whole period the product/service has been offered, based on complete 12-month periods.
source_quote: the information must include appropriate performance information which covers the immediately preceding 5 years, or the whole period for which the financial instrument has been offered... and in every case that performance information must be based on complete 12-month periods;

requirement: Marketing information must clearly state the reference period and the source of past performance information.
source_quote: the reference period and the source of information must be clearly stated;

requirement: Marketing information containing past performance must include a prominent warning that past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results.
source_quote: the information must contain a prominent warning that the figures refer to the past and that past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results;

requirement: If past performance figures are denominated in a currency other than that of the client’s Member State, the currency must be clearly stated with a warning about currency fluctuation risks.
source_quote: where the indication relies on figures denominated in a currency other than that of the Member State in which the retail client or potential retail client is resident, the currency must be clearly stated, together with a warning that the return may increase or decrease as a result of currency fluctuations;

requirement: If past performance is based on gross performance, the effect of commissions, fees or other charges must be disclosed.
source_quote: where the indication is based on gross performance, the effect of commissions, fees or other charges must be disclosed.

requirement: Marketing information including simulated past performance must relate to a financial instrument or index and comply with conditions for actual past performance disclosures.
source_quote: the simulated past performance must be based on the actual past performance of one or more financial instruments or financial indices... the conditions set out in points (a) to (c), (e) and (f) of subparagraph 4 must be complied with;

requirement: Marketing information with simulated past performance must contain a prominent warning that the figures refer to simulated past performance and that past performance is not a reliable indicator of future performance.
source_quote: the information must contain a prominent warning that the figures refer to simulated past performance and that past performance is not a reliable indicator of future performance.

requirement: Marketing information containing future performance forecasts must not be based on or refer to simulated past performance.
source_quote: the information must not be based on or refer to simulated past performance;

requirement: Future performance information must be based on reasonable assumptions supported by objective data.
source_quote: the information must be based on reasonable assumptions supported by objective data;

requirement: If future performance information is based on gross performance, the effect of commissions, fees or other charges must be disclosed.
source_quote: where the information is based on gross performance, the effect of commissions, fees or other charges must be disclosed;

requirement: Marketing information with future performance forecasts must contain a prominent warning that such forecasts are not a reliable indicator of future performance.
source_quote: the information must contain a prominent warning that such forecasts are not a reliable indicator of future performance

requirement: Marketing information referring to a particular tax treatment must prominently state that the tax treatment depends on individual client circumstances and may change in the future.
source_quote: Where the information refers to a particular tax treatment, it shall prominently state that the tax treatment depends on the individual circumstances of each client and may be subject to change in the future.

requirement: Marketing information shall not use the name of any competent authority in a way that suggests endorsement or approval of the products or services of the investment firm.
source_quote: The information shall not use the name of any competent authority in such a way that would indicate or suggest endorsement or approval by that authority of the products or services of the IF.
